transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... they told me to come. Said my talking gets... mixed up. Like, I try to tell them about the keys, you know? And then... the jail. The prayer rug. Chess pieces. And they just... they say they can't follow me. So I'm here.

When you're talking about these things—the keys, the jail, the prayer rug—do your thoughts feel like they're moving really fast, like you can't keep up with them? Or does it feel more like your thoughts are getting tangled or disconnected from each other?

They just go fast, I guess. ...Like a whole crowd talking inside my head all at once. I can't catch them. It just jumps from the bills... to the jail... the mosque... the cleaning chemicals from work. Just... runs too fast to catch a single one.
During the time when your thoughts are racing like this, how is your mood? Are you feeling unusually happy or energized, or are you feeling more anxious, scared, or down?

I don't know... mostly just... energized, I guess. Sometimes I feel really good. Like, really powerful. I'll be laughing, talking loud to whoever's around. But... then someone will say something wrong, or question what I'm doing, and... I just snap. I get so mad over nothing. I'll just start shouting. It just... happens.
How long have you been feeling this way—the racing thoughts, the energy, the mood changes? Has it been going on for a few days, a couple of weeks, or longer?
I don't know... a while. It comes and goes. If you add it all up, the times when I'm up like that, not sleeping, having all these plans... maybe a year and eight months. Total. I guess.
When you're having these racing thoughts and feeling powerful, do you ever hear voices or see things that other people don't hear or see? Or do you believe things that others tell you aren't true?

Yeah... I guess so. When I'm up like that, not sleeping much, figuring out all the plans for the buildings... that's when I hear the voice in the vent. And... I just know the hallway lights are blinking out warnings. About me. People say it's just bad wiring, but... I know what it means.

When you're feeling normal—not energized, not up like that—do you still hear the voice in the vent or see the hallway lights blinking with warnings? Or do those things only happen when you're in that energized state?

Yeah... sometimes. Even when I'm... just regular. Not wired, not down. Just... working. 

There was a stretch... maybe a couple weeks, more than two weeks, I think. I was feeling pretty calm. But... I still heard the man in the vents. And... I still knew they were signaling about me in the building. So... yeah. It still happens.

During that couple of weeks when you were feeling calm and sleeping normally—not energized, not down—were you still hearing that voice in the vents and seeing those warning signals the whole time, or did they go away during that period?

Yeah. I just said that. I was fine... not high, not depressed. But the man was still there. For more than two weeks, he was still talking in the vents. And I still knew they were signaling. It didn't stop.

When you were feeling calm and sleeping normally during those two weeks, did you also feel like your thoughts were racing or hard to follow? Or was it just the voice and the signals, but your thinking was clear?

No... they still go fast. Even when I'm calm. 

It's just... like a whole crowd talking inside my head. Jumping around all over. I'll be thinking about my bills, and then... jail, or the mosque... or the cleaning chemicals I use at work. Just running so fast I can't even catch one of them. So... no, my head wasn't clear.

Looking back to when this all started—way at the beginning—did you hear that voice in the vents or notice those warning signals before you ever started having the racing thoughts and feeling really energized? Or did the voice and signals show up around the same time as the energy and fast thoughts?

I don't really remember the exact start of it all. But... yeah. When I was only sleeping a few hours a night... and I was making all those big plans for the buildings... I was hearing him then, too. The voice in the vent. And I was sure the hallway lights were warning me. So... they were happening together.

You mentioned that even when you're feeling calm and sleeping normally, you still hear the man in the vents and notice the hallway lights signaling. During those calm periods with normal sleep, are you also feeling energized or powerful like you described before? Or is it just the voice and signals happening while your mood feels regular?

No... when I'm calm, I'm just calm. 

The... the energized stuff is different. That's when I feel... big. Powerful. I get loud, talking to everybody, laughing. But... I don't know, if someone looks at me wrong or asks too many questions, I get... I snap at them. Yell over nothing. But that's not when I'm calm. That's... the other time.

During those calm periods when you're sleeping normally and not feeling energized or powerful—just regular—how many days or weeks at a time would you say the voice in the vents is there? Is it there every single day, or does it come and go?

It's... it's there every day. 

Even when I'm just... regular. Not high up, not down in a hole. Just working. I'll go weeks like that, maybe... more than two weeks, where I'm just normal. But he's still there. The man in the vents. And the people signaling... they don't stop just because I'm feeling calm. It's... it just keeps going. Every day.
